assertion.quantifiers: For every retained known simple-zero pair (h,k) satisfying the stated splitting, coprimality and old-local-type conditions.
assertion.uniformity: No new global uniformity claim; the exact identities retain every local factor.
assertion.constants: All component factors and torsion orders are retained before taking valuations.
assertion.limit_order: Apply at the finite known simple-zero constituents before any limiting calibration inference.
assertion.objects: At each companion p|k, good E0=E^(h) over F=Q_p, tame ramified quadratic L=K_p, ramified twist E0^(k), and Res_{L/F}(E0_L).
assertion.hypotheses: p odd, E0 good, L/F totally ramified quadratic, mu2 contained in the base DVR. h,k and old support satisfy the stated splitting conditions.
assertion.parameter_range: All companion primes; exclude residue characteristic2 and old bad primes from this tame calculation.
assertion.normalizations: Component number means #Phi(F_p), not #Phi over the algebraic closure. Preserve the finite étale residue-field group scheme and its Frobenius action. Twisting by h acts trivially on E[2].
assertion.exceptional_cases: t_p=dim_F2 E[2]^Frob_p generally; it equals2 only because all E[2] is rational here. No tame formula at p=2, no replacement of rational by geometric component counts. The global product and its sign in the determinant coordinate are later deductions.
assertion.statement: At each stated odd companion prime, the ramified twist component group is the finite etale residue-field group E0_tilde[2], while the Weil restriction of the good model has connected special fiber and component number one.

use.reason: Exact source-side application before multiplying local component factors.

supplier.statement: For tame totally ramified cyclic degree n with mu_n in the DVR, Edixhoven gives a Néron special-fiber filtration with Gr0=(A′_k)^mu_n and positive graded terms vector groups. Thus F1 is connected and Phi is pi0((A′_k)^mu_n). Proposition4.1 identifies the Weil restriction of the Néron model with the Néron model of the restricted variety; §5.1 identifies its reduction kernel and graded vector-group terms.
